questions.stem:
Given the strict mathematical statement: A > B = C < D. Which of the following clear conclusions rigidly logically follows?
Conclusions:
I. A > C
II. B < D
questions.explanation: From the statement: A > B = C. Therefore, replacing B with C gives A > C. So, I follows. From B = C < D, replacing C with B gives B < D. So, II follows. Both follow.

questions.stem:
Given the strict mathematical statement: P ≤ Q < R = S. Which of the following clear conclusions rigidly logically follows?
Conclusions:
I. P < S
II. Q < S
questions.explanation: From the statement: P ≤ Q < R = S. The relationship between P and S involves a '<' sign, which overrides the '≤'. So, P < S. Thus, I follows. Also, Q < R = S means Q < S. Thus, II follows. Both follow.

questions.stem:
Given the strict mathematical statement: M ≥ N = O > P ≤ Q. Which of the following clear conclusions rigidly logically follows?
Conclusions:
I. M > P
II. N < Q
questions.explanation: For I: M ≥ N = O > P. The signs are aligned (≥, =, >). The dominant sign is '>'. So, M > P. Thus, I follows. For II: N = O > P ≤ Q. The signs between N and Q are opposing (>, ≤). No definite relationship can be established between N and Q. Thus, II does not follow.

questions.stem:
Given the strict mathematical statement: X < Y ≤ Z = W ≥ V. Which of the following clear conclusions rigidly logically follows?
Conclusions:
I. X < W
II. Y ≥ V
questions.explanation: For I: X < Y ≤ Z = W. The signs are aligned and the dominant sign is '<'. So, X < W. Thus, I follows. For II: Y ≤ Z = W ≥ V. The signs between Y and V are opposing (≤, ≥). No definite relationship can be established. Thus, II does not follow.

questions.stem:
Given the strict mathematical statements: D = E > F ≥ G; F < H. Which of the following clear conclusions rigidly logically follows?
Conclusions:
I. D > G
II. E < H
questions.explanation: For I: D = E > F ≥ G. The dominant sign is '>'. Therefore, D > G. I follows. For II: combining statements, E > F < H. The signs between E and H are opposing (>, <). Therefore, no relationship can be determined between E and H. II does not follow.

questions.stem:
Given the strict mathematical statements: J ≥ K > L = M < N; O ≤ L. Which of the following clear conclusions rigidly logically follows?
Conclusions:
I. J > O
II. N > O
questions.explanation: For I: We know J ≥ K > L. From the second statement, O ≤ L, which is the same as L ≥ O. Combining: J ≥ K > L ≥ O. The dominant sign is '>'. So, J > O. I follows. For II: We know N > M. Since M = L, N > L. From L ≥ O, combining gives N > L ≥ O. Dominant sign is '>'. So, N > O. II follows. Both follow.

questions.stem:
Given the strict mathematical statements: S ≤ T = U < V ≥ W; U > X. Which of the following clear conclusions rigidly logically follows?
Conclusions:
I. V > X
II. S < V
questions.explanation: For I: We know V > U. From the second statement, U > X. Combining gives V > U > X. So, V > X. I follows. For II: From the main statement, S ≤ T = U < V. The dominant sign here is '<'. Therefore, S < V. II follows. Both follow.
